title: Manthara
hook: a battlefield promise the king forgot, and a maid who remembered

segments.voice: Yesterday: Manthara painted a picture of the future, and Kaikeyi, after a fight, gave way. Did you ask what had actually happened so far? Today, Manthara brings out an old promise. A new week begins. Day five hundred nineteen.

Years earlier, long before Rama was born, the gods were at war with a demon named Shambara, and they asked King Dasharatha to fight on their side. Kaikeyi rode with him. In the battle the king was badly wounded and fell unconscious. Kaikeyi drove his chariot out of the fighting and saved his life. When he woke, he was grateful enough to say: ask me for two things, anything. Kaikeyi said, I'll ask later. And then, it seems, she forgot about it. Manthara didn't.
screen: `A WAR WITH SHAMBARA.` → `KAIKEYI SAVES THE KING.` → `ASK ME FOR TWO THINGS.`

segments.voice: Kaikeyi asks Manthara how to stop the coronation, and Manthara answers by reminding her of her own story. Don't you remember? You told it to me yourself. The king owes you two boons. Now's the time. Ask for two things. First, that Bharata be consecrated as heir. Second, that Rama be sent to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years, living as an ascetic. Fourteen years, Manthara reasons, is long enough for Bharata to win the people's hearts and put down roots. Then she gives Kaikeyi a plan, step by step. Go to the anger room, the room where a queen goes when she's wronged. Take off your jewels. Put on soiled clothes. Lie on the bare floor. When the king comes, don't look at him, don't speak. He can't bear to see you upset. He'll offer you gems and gold. Refuse them. Make him swear first, and only then ask. It's an unsettling speech, because it's so practical. Manthara knows the king's heart better than he does. She knows his love for Kaikeyi, and his pride in keeping his word, and she builds the trap out of those two good things. Kaikeyi, fully won now, praises Manthara warmly and promises her gold ornaments when Bharata rules. Then she does exactly what she's been told. She goes into the anger room, strips off her jewelry, scatters it on the floor, and lies down on the bare floor. And that's where Manthara's part in the plot is complete. The rest will be done by a promise.
screen: `THE KING OWES YOU TWO BOONS.` · `BHARATA CROWNED, RAMA TO THE FOREST.` · `GO TO THE ANGER ROOM.` · `A TRAP MADE OF GOOD THINGS.` · then, large: `THE REST WILL BE DONE BY A PROMISE.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably. Think of a promise someone made to you that you've never collected, or one you made that someone else still holds. Don't decide anything about it. Just hold it lightly in mind, and notice how it feels to carry it. On each breath out, let the shoulders drop. Promises are heavy things. Today, simply notice the weight. The bell holds the time.
Manthara. The maid who remembers the king's forgotten battlefield promise, and turns it, with a careful plan, into a trap.
Your line: Manthara. Today, think about one promise you've made, and whether you'd still want it kept the way it was asked. Day five hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: The kopa-griha, or anger room, appears in this episode of the Ayodhya Kanda; storytellers often pause here to point out how Manthara builds her plan from the king's love and his pride in keeping his word.

match.prompt: the old promise — tap the pairs.
pairs: drove the wounded king to safety
where a wronged queen lies down

myth: the boons were a wedding gift
they were the king's thanks for saving his life in battle.
Manthara tells Kaikeyi to refuse gifts and make the king swear first
that's the heart of her plan.
the plan asks for Rama to be sent away forever
it asks for fourteen years in the Dandaka forest.

fork.setup: you're Kaikeyi, now convinced. Manthara has given you a plan. what do you do?
options: talk to the king calmly tonight.
go to the anger room and lie on the floor.
fork.reveal: she strips off her jewels, scatters them, and lies on the bare floor of the anger room, and waits for the king.

original.note: Sanskrit krodhāgāra: the anger room, from krodha, anger, and āgāra, room or house.

trapdoor: what you thought: Kaikeyi invented the boons on the spot.
what it means: they were real, given after she saved the king in the war with Shambara, and Manthara reminded her.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki gives the fourteen-year term inside Manthara's plan, with a political reason: long enough for Bharata to take root.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 9 (the Shambara war; the two boons; Manthara's plan; the anger room)

notes: Sarga number follows the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Details of the Shambara war (Kaikeyi drives the wounded, unconscious king from the field): confirm. Some versions have her repairing the chariot; that version is not used.
Manthara's reason for fourteen years (Bharata takes root): paraphrased; confirm.
Kaikeyi's praise of Manthara (including remarks about her hump) is softened to 'praises her warmly and promises gold ornaments'.
Valmiki's simile for Kaikeyi lying on the floor is left out because its wording could not be confirmed.
